blocks.content: Understanding the Earth's interior is essential for comprehending surface landforms, seismic hazards, and the geomagnetic field that sustains life.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Studying the Earth's interior helps explain endogenic processes, tectonic forces, and surface geomorphology.
Direct sources of information include deep mining and volcanic materials, while indirect sources rely on seismic wave behavior, gravity, and magnetic anomalies.
Convection currents in the asthenosphere act as the primary engine behind plate tectonics and continental drift.
The liquid outer core creates Earth's geomagnetic field via geodynamo action, protecting the atmosphere from solar winds.
Density and composition changes within internal layers account for Earth's gravitational variations and heat budget.
Seismic Discontinuities: Mohorovičić (Crust-Mantle), Gutenberg (Mantle-Outer Core), and Lehmann (Outer-Inner Core) are frequently asked in UPSC/State PCS exams.
S-waves cannot travel through liquids, which proves that Earth's outer core is in a molten state.
P-wave shadow zone forms between 103° and 142° from the epicenter, while the S-wave shadow zone extends continuously beyond 103°.
